newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian 2009 bond finds reasonable demand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian 2009 bond finds reasonable demand.

text.p: Australian bonds saw reasonable demand for a new line of stock at today's A$800 million two-tranche Treasury bond tender, but failed to make much impression on a weakened market, traders said.

The A$600 million of 7.5 percent September 2009 stock went off at an average yield of 7.572 percent at its debut tender compared with around 7.53/7.49 percent seen quoted for the August 2008 stock just prior to the result.
"It's not a bad result, given the size of the tender for a new stock," said one trader at a European based bank.

However, "the 2002 looks like a bit of a disaster, but I think that's just a reflection of all the concern being on the 2009, and people just leaving it for someone else to bid for it," the trader added.

The A$200 million March 2002 bond fetched an average yield of 7.153 percent compared with around 7.155/7.115 percent seen quoted for the existing stock when final bids went in, while accepted bids were a wide 7.13 to 7.20 percent.
By 2.45 p.m. (0345 GMT), the December 10-year bond futures contract was 92.545, only marginally above the 92.540 seen before the tender result.

The tender is the fourth instalment of the Treasury's T-bond issuance programme for the 1996/97 fiscal year, bringing supply to some A$3.0 billion, including A$200 million in the 2009 stock taken up by the RBA for its own portfolio.
At the time of the August 20 budget, the Treasury projected total T-bond issuance for the financial year at A$6.0 to A$7.0 billion.

The market weakened during the morning as it made room for the new supply and after U.S. Treasuries softened on Monday ahead of a string U.S. economic indicators this week, starting with September quarter employment cost index later today.
However, there is an inherent underlying bid tone in the market on the expectation that monetary policy would be eased next week after the Reserve Bank board meets on Tuesday.
A 50 basis point easing in current 7.0 percent official interest rates remains full priced in.
